articles.summary: Northern California leg of Archer’s No Roads Tour wraps up as Midnight heads south to Los Angeles Archer's all-electric Midnight air taxi recently completed a week filled with piloted flights across Northern California, including multiple flights around the San Francisco Bay that took off and landed at Oakland International Airport. ( Watch Video ) The Bay Area flights capped Archer’s month-long Northern California leg of its ‘No Roads’ flight tour showcasing its Midnight air taxi making stops in Hollister, San Martin, San Jose, Mountain View and Hayward before arriving in Oakland. The purpose of the Northern California leg of Archer’s ‘No Roads’ tour was to showcase Midnight’s ability to operate seamlessly in complex urban airspace surrounding the Bay Area's three international airports — San Francisco, Oakland and San Jose. articles.title: Archer Completes Historic Electric Air Taxi Flights Over San Francisco Bay

articles.summary: Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) and ITA Airways, member of the Lufthansa Group, Europe's largest airline group, announced today that they have signed an agreement to partner on an all-electric air taxi network in Italy. ITA Airways is Italy's flag carrier, serving more than 70 destinations worldwide as part of the Star Alliance network. A rendering of Archer’s all-electric Midnight air taxi flying in Italy Using Archer's Midnight aircraft, the partnership will look to deploy air taxi services in major cities across Italy. Designed for rapid back-to-back flights with zero-operating emissions, the goal of Archer’s Midnight aircraft is to transform urban travel by replacing 60–90 minutes drives with quiet, all-electric flights of 10–20 minutes. For example, an hour-long trip on the ground from Fiumicino Airport to Rome’s city center could take less than 10 minutes with a flight in Midnight. articles.summary: Archer unveiled plans for air taxi networks across three cities of the Texas Triangle — with the goal of giving Texans in America’s fastest growing megaregion a way to skip traffic and turn hour-long drives into 10–20 minute flights on its all-electric Midnight air taxi. Archer's planned network in Dallas–Fort Worth would link the Metroplex’s major airports to the region's business districts, including Frisco Station, in partnership with Hillwood, founded by Ross Perot Jr. In Houston, home to some of the nation's worst congestion, Archer’s planned air taxi network aims to connect the city's major airports to its business centers and coastal destinations, from the beaches of Galveston to downtown hotel properties like the Thompson Hotel Helipad. The network in Austin aims to connect the city's major airports like Austin-Bergstrom International Airport and the helipad at the Circuit of the Americas (COTA), home to the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix. articles.title: Archer Unveils Texas Air Taxi Networks Across Houston, Dallas, and Austin
